trade_offs.description: Every source table becomes its own collection, and the notes table is embedded in the reviewables collection as an array named notes, capped at 50 entries.
trade_offs.impact: A reviewable and its notes load in one read, and clearing a user's notes is one update. The cap is enforced by the application, because the database does not limit array length.

trade_offs.description: Columns that point at users, posts, topics, categories and groups become plain id fields, because those parent tables are served by other engines.
trade_offs.impact: The database no longer checks these references or joins across them. The application resolves them with separate reads and removes orphaned references itself.

trade_offs.description: Three joins are served with one equality lookup stage each: form templates through category links, themes through child links, and user API keys through their client.
trade_offs.impact: Each read runs a single lookup into a small collection. The pipelines were written for the equality form that runs on every DocumentDB version, and no pipeline chains two lookups.

trade_offs.description: Filters that use not-equal, not-in or a negated pattern cannot use an index for that condition: the translation override status test, the token log action exclusion, and the not-null test on rejected emails.
trade_offs.impact: Each query still starts from an index on its other fields, and the remaining condition is checked on the documents that scan returns. These collections hold tens of documents in the source statistics, so the extra check is cheap.

trade_offs.description: The sidebar sections order uses a computed expression, so the pipeline computes a flag and sorts on it after the index matches the public sections.
trade_offs.impact: The sort runs in memory on the matched sections, which are few. No index can serve this order.

trade_offs.description: Two source statements test a column against null where the column cannot be null, and one tests the primary key against null. They return no rows.
trade_offs.impact: The design keeps them as written so every statement stays covered, and the application can remove these calls.

trade_offs.description: Indexes are listed for the observed queries and the primary key only. Source unique constraints that no access pattern names (for example on sitemaps.name and uploads.sha1) are not in the list.
trade_offs.impact: Create those as unique indexes before data load, or duplicates will be accepted. This adds write cost on those collections, which hold small row counts.

trade_offs.description: The color scheme insert no longer gets a database-generated id.
trade_offs.impact: The application supplies the _id on insert. Existing ids are copied from the source so references stay valid.

trade_offs.description: Source timestamps become ISODate values, network address columns become strings, JSON columns become sub-documents, array columns become native arrays, and the sprite bytes column becomes binary data.
trade_offs.impact: Date and JSON queries work on typed fields. Address columns lose the network type, so range or subnet matching moves to the application.

trade_offs.description: Row counts for most tables are not in the source statistics, so the figures use the stated assumption of size over declared row width. The api_keys average of 71.68 KB comes from its address array column.
trade_offs.impact: Every collection is far below the 16 MB document limit. The largest are api_keys at 71.68 KB, sitemaps at 17.07 KB and ai_mcp_servers at 14.8 KB. Sizes should be rechecked against real data after load.

trade_offs.description: The API key lookup is the busiest statement at 3.27 requests per second and reads the whole document, so its index is on the hash and _id and does not cover the read.
trade_offs.impact: One index lookup plus one document fetch per call. A covering index is not used because the statement returns every column.

trade_offs.description: The themes collection has an index on color_scheme_id, which routing assumed for the color scheme lookup.
trade_offs.impact: The lookup by color scheme reads through that key instead of scanning themes. It adds one index write per theme update.

trade_offs.description: The source extension functions (text matching, key-value, vector and case-insensitive text helpers) and the three trigger functions belong to tables that other engines serve, so none move with this design.
trade_offs.impact: No stored logic needs replacing for the collections in this design.
